pages.text: Welcome to our classroom! Today is the start of a very special mission. My name is Melody Moo, and I am a little monster who loves the planet. "Look at the board!" I say to my friends. We are starting the Zero Waste Challenge. We want to reduce, reuse, and recycle every day!

"Show me your notebook," I tell my friend Page. A notebook is a precious thing! To reduce waste, we must use every single piece of paper from the front to the back. Do not leave any blank spaces! "Write on both sides of every page!"

Page is busy coloring a beautiful poster. "Give me the felt tip pens when you are finished," I say. We must make sure the caps are on tight so they do not dry out. If they stay juicy, we can use them for a long, long time. Reuse is about taking care of what we already have!

"Find your ruler and your glue stick," I suggest to Page. We looked in our old backpacks from last year and found so many things! We don't need new ones every year. My ruler is a bit scratched, and Page's glue stick is almost finished, but they still work perfectly.

Sometimes we have big books that we all need to use. "Pass me the dictionary," I ask. We only need one dictionary for the whole table. By sharing, we reduce the number of things we need to own. "Share your resources with your neighbors!"

Page is organizing his desk. "Put your highlighter inside your folder," I instruct him. When we keep our supplies organized, we don't lose them. If we lose a highlighter, we have to buy a new one, and that creates more waste.

Math class is starting. "Give me the calculator for a moment," I say as I check my equations. Our calculators use batteries, so we must use them wisely. When a calculator breaks, we try to fix it instead of throwing it away. "Value your gadgets," I tell my friends.

Now it is time to tidy up the room. We have three special bins. "Help me sort the trash," I say to Page. Paper goes in one bin, plastic in another, and scraps in the third. "Recycle everything you can!" we shout together. We are making sure that nothing useful is wasted.

Our school is a bright and modern place with big glass windows that let the sun shine in. As we walk outside, I look back at our classroom. "Join our challenge!" I call out to everyone. With our notebooks, rulers, and folders, we are making a big difference for the planet!
